newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Indian GDRs edge up in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Indian GDRs edge up in thin trade.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts ended mildly firmer in quiet trade on Monday as the market continued to struggle amid limited direction from local stocks, traders and brokers said.
They reported thin volumes on the day, after Bombay stocks ended flat. The market was expected to focus on the 1997/8 budget, which is due to go to parliament this week.
Four leading left-wing parties on Monday said they would be looking for changes in the budget in certain areas, including taxes and divestment in public enterprises.
"We have really only seen some fiddling with prices today," a broker said. "The focus is on the budget and whether the left wing parties create any problems."
He said premiums in the market remained relatively high and were keeping a lid on the GDR market until local stock prices offered fresh direction.
Reliance picked up 25 cents to $19.25/$19.75 and Hindalco made six cents to $32.00/$33.00.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 0.81 points up at 80.90, with the premium over the local market at 21.05 percent from 19.78 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index dipped 0.06 points to 3,825.51.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index added 0.43 points to 131.11, representing a discount to the local market of 1.69 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index tracked gains in local stocks, rising 1.53 points, or 2.43 percent, to 64.66, a premium of 31.06 percent over the local market.
